title: Attributable latency slices and incident telemetry bridge
creator: Michael Chen
description: Problem: Our current SLO and burn-rate alerts surface aggregate latency and error signals but lack stable attribution into request-path slices and trace-linked evidence. On-call frequently gets noisy pages that are hard to triage (multiple services implicated) and we waste cycles chasing false-positive bursts. Goal: build an "incident telemetry bridge" that joins span-level tracing hooks to the metric/log pipeline, emit pre-aggregated, attributable latency slices (by route, model, plan tier, region) and a lightweight evidence bundle (top spans + sample trace id) attached to alerts so paging and incident triage is fast and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Alerts for burn-rate and latency include an "evidence bundle" with top 3 contributing spans and a sample trace id. 2) New latency-slice metrics (route/model/region/plan) are available in metrics store and dashboards (with 1m and 5m rollups). 3) On-call noise decreases: >30% reduction in duplicate pages for the same root cause in canary teams over 4 weeks. 4) No higher than 5% additional ingestion cost for traces; metrics pipeline stays within budget during spike tests.
design_summary: - Add lightweight tracing hook in serving runtime to emit 'slice keys' and span fingerprints. - Enrich metrics pipeline (kafka -> aggregator) to accept trace-linked envelopes and produce per-slice latency histograms and top-span counters. - Extend alert payload to include evidence bundle (list of span signatures + sample trace link). - Dashboard templates for deterministic slice-based SLOs and an 'attribution' panel that shows top contributors to burn. - Provide a feature flag and rollout in three phases: test-only, internal canary, org-wide.
implementation_notes: - Runtime change: add trace-envelope protobuf (minimal) and batching to avoid per-request RTT hit. - Pipeline: new topic 'trace-attrib' consumed by aggregator workers with idempotent processing. - Storage: use metrics TSDB for histogram buckets and a small bounded LRU store (redis) for sample trace links. - Alerting: modify burn-rate alert generator to attach sample evidence by querying the LRU store at alert time if present, otherwise attach the aggregated top-span counters.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: tracing envelope increases network and ingestion costs. Mitigation: envelope is configurable (sampling ratio and route-based whitelist) and defaults to 1% globally. - Risk: added pipeline complexity could delay alerting. Mitigation: pipeline is eventually consistent for attribution; alerts still fire based on metrics alone and evidence is best-effort. - Risk: privacy/PII in traces. Mitigation: strip payloads at runtime; only span names, durations, and hashed identifiers are sent.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): runtime hook behind flag + 1% global sampling to 'trace-attrib' topic; internal test team only. Phase 2 (Week 2-3): increase sampling to 5% for canary services and add aggregator workers; enable dashboard panels. Phase 3 (Week 4): org-wide enable with route-based sampling and default retention. Monitor ingestion and latency metrics throughout.
test_plan: - Unit tests for trace-envelope encoding/decoding. - Load test simulating 2x peak QPS to verify <5% ingestion increase. - Canary: enable for billing and inference-route 'chat' for 72 hours and verify alert evidence appears and pages reduce. - Post-rollout: 30-day comparison of duplicate page rate and mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for canary teams.
monitoring_and_success_metrics: - Duplicate page rate (same root-cause cluster within 15m): target -30% for canaries. - MTTA: target -20% reduction. - Evidence attach rate: >70% of burn-rate alerts include an evidence bundle. - Ingestion cost delta: <5% increase vs baseline.
open_questions: What default sampling ratio is acceptable for Dedicated customers (who expect no external telemetry)?
Should evidence bundles include synthetic spans from prefix cache operations (they are high-frequency)?
Do we want to surface the attribution scoring algorithm in the UI or keep it hidden as implementation detail?
